title: H4G: Unlocking Faithful Inference for Zero-Shot Graph Learning in Hyperbolic Space

problem.claim: Zero-shot graph learning on text-attributed graphs requires fine-grained pattern recognition, especially for heterophilic graphs.

gap.claim: Existing methods use excessively large hyperbolic radii, compressing multi-scale structural information into uniform high-level abstractions and obscuring critical local patterns.

contributions.claim: H4G systematically reduces hyperbolic embedding radii using learnable block-diagonal scaling matrices and Möbius matrix multiplication.
The framework targets faithful preservation of fine-grained structural details while maintaining global receptive ability with minimal computational overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, including a 12.8% improvement on heterophilic graphs.
Experiments report an 8.4% improvement on homophilic graphs.
The authors report that radius reduction enables faithful multi-scale representation for zero-shot graph learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Text-attributed graphs support zero-shot learning through graph-text alignment.
Existing methods struggle with fine-grained pattern recognition, particularly on heterophilic graphs.
Large hyperbolic radii cause over-abstraction and loss of local structural information.
H4G reduces embedding radii with learnable scaling and Möbius matrix multiplication while preserving global receptive ability.
Experiments report improvements on heterophilic and homophilic graphs.

source_observation.claim: The abstract attributes performance limitations to excessive hyperbolic radii that compress multi-scale structure.

interpretation.claim: Representation scale should be treated as a controllable factor when fine-grained structural information matters.

application.claim: For hyperbolic graph representations, evaluate whether reducing embedding radii improves local-pattern retention without sacrificing global context.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether radius reduction benefits graph types or tasks beyond the reported settings.
